 Drunks, Lovers, Sinners and Saints: Blackhawks vs. Kings Preview
 A stretch of seven games at the UC concludes this evening. 
 Posted on October 27, 2026 October 27, 2026 by Dave Melton 
 (Photo by Melissa Tamez/Icon Sportswire) 
 The Hawks come to the end of a home-heavy stretch of their schedule in desperate need of a win as they host the Los Angeles Kings on Tuesday night at the United Center. 
 Just one week ago, everything was pretty awful for the Kings as well following an 0-4-2 start to the season. The mood has lightened recently, though, thanks to three wins in four games during a five-game road trip that ends with this visit to Chicago, a decent flight from a 6-3 victory over the Rangers in New York on Monday night. Although LA is riding higher than it was, the Kings will probably have some heavy legs to start this game.
 Those wins have come in spite of a rash of injuries for the Kings. Kevin Fiala still hasn’t played this season following an injury late last season. Alex Turcotte, the No. 5 pick in 2019, went on injured reserve earlier this month while Mats Zuccarello, a free-agent signing this summer, went on IR earlier this week. Quinton Byfield, the No. 2 pick in 2020, was briefly sidelined before returning to the ice on Monday, yet he has just a pair of points (1 G, 1 A) this season.
 What this team does have is a healthy Artemi Panarin, who leads the Kings in goals (7) and points (11) through 10 games. Additional points have come his linemates up front in Alex Laferriere (2 G, 7 A) and Adrian Kempe (3 G, 5 A), while the back-end production is primarily from youngster Brandt Clarke (3 G, 5 A). Drew Doughty has just four points this season, with three of them coming on Monday night. The top line for LA has caught fire in the last week and remains the largest threat this team can muster, although it’s fair to wonder how long that fire can keep this offense burning without support from somewhere else.
 In net, neither Darcy Kuemper (3-3-1 record, .889 save percentage, 3.47 goals-against average) nor old friend Anton Forsberg (0-2-1, .894, 2.48) offer significant resistance. Kuemper played on Monday night, so the expectation is for Forsberg to be in net for this game. That is probably the only lineup change to expect from what took the ice against the Rangers.

— lineslineslines.bsky.social ( @lineslineslines.bsky.social ) October 26, 2026 at 5:37 PM 
 As for the Hawks, their season continues trending in all of the wrong directions. Chicago’s lost three in a row and wraps up a seven-game homestand this evening with only one regulation win tallied from the first six. An OT win over the Jets makes the 2-4 record from this home-heavy stretch look marginally better, yet even a third win tonight will feel slightly underwhelming — similar to the theme of the whole season thus far.
 Must-win games aren’t a thing in October for the Hawks but this one feels pretty close to that, given how poorly things have started and the desperate need for some positivity before a crunch of games largely on the road unfolds over the next few weeks. A lineup shuffle precedes this game, with the most notable changes among the forward group, where Oliver Moore appears set for a return while Andrew Mangiapane seems to be press-boxed. He’ll team up with fellow speedster Frank Nazar while Patrick Kane joins them on the second line. Ryan Greene jumps up to the top line with Roman Kantserov and Connor Bedard while Anton Frondell is flanked by Tyler Bertuzzi and Ryan Donato on the third line. The fourth line sees Teuvo take Greene’s alongside Cole Smith and Jordan Greenway. 
 On defense, Bowen Byram remains out with an injury, so the pairings were largely unchanged from the last game, which means Kevin Korchinski plays but Ethan Del Mastro likely does not. And Spencer Knight looks to be the goalie based on the morning skate.

 Not much else to say other than the Hawks just need to win a damn game already. 
 Let’s go Hawks.
